subject: math
title: Grade 6 One-Step Equations
seo_title: Grade 6 One-Step Equations Worksheets: Free Math with Answer Key (BC Curriculum)
standard_text: One-step equations with whole-number coefficients and solutions
meta_desc: Free Grade 6 math worksheets on one-step equations for the BC curriculum: pan balances, solving x + 12 = 30, 5x = 35 and x ÷ 4 = 8 with inverse operations, and writing and solving equations from stories. 100 questions with an answer key.
key_big: Use the inverse operation on both sides: subtraction undoes addition, and division undoes multiplication.
key_sub: 5x = 35, so x = 35 ÷ 5 = 7. x ÷ 4 = 8, so x = 8 × 4 = 32. Then check by putting the answer back in.
body_html:
An equation is a balance

An equation says two sides are equal, like a level pan balance. A letter such as x stands for the unknown number. To solve the equation, find the value of x that makes it true.

Use the inverse operation

Undo what is done to x. Use the inverse operation, and do it to both sides. Then put your answer back in to check.

EquationUndo it withDo thisAnswer
x + 12 = 30− 12 on both sides30 − 12x = 18
x − 9 = 20+ 9 on both sides20 + 9x = 29
5x = 35÷ 5 on both sides35 ÷ 5x = 7
x ÷ 4 = 8× 4 on both sides8 × 4x = 32

5x means 5 × x. A number written right before a letter means multiply.

Example

x ÷ 4 = 8

x is the number you start with. Multiply both sides by 4: x = 8 × 4 = 32. Check: 32 ÷ 4 = 8.

Answer: x = 32

Example

x + 12 500 = 30 000

Subtract 12 500 from both sides: x = 30 000 − 12 500 = 17 500. Check: 17 500 + 12 500 = 30 000.

Answer: x = 17 500

Write an equation from a story

Choose a letter for the number you do not know. Joining is +, taking away is −, equal groups are ×, and sharing equally is ÷. Then solve and check.

Example

4 SkyTrain cars carry 520 people. Each car carries the same number. How many in each car?

Equation: 4p = 520. Divide both sides by 4: p = 130. Check: 4 × 130 = 520.

Answer: 130 people

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
x + 12 = 30, so x = 42 (30 + 12)Use the inverse: 30 − 12 = 18
x − 9 = 20, so x = 11 (20 − 9)Use the inverse: 20 + 9 = 29
5x = 35, so x = 175 (35 × 5)Use the inverse: 35 ÷ 5 = 7
5x = 35, so x = 30 (35 − 5)5x means 5 × x, so divide
x ÷ 4 = 8, so x = 2 (8 ÷ 4)Use the inverse: 8 × 4 = 32
Changing only one sideDo the same to both sides to keep the balance level

faq.q: What are one-step equations in Grade 6 math in BC?
faq.a: They are equations like x + 12 = 30, 5x = 35 or x ÷ 4 = 8 that take one step to solve. The BC Grade 6 Patterning standard uses whole-number coefficients and whole-number solutions.
5x means 5 × x, so use the inverse operation and divide both sides by 5: x = 35 ÷ 5 = 7. Check by putting 7 back in: 5 × 7 = 35.

faq.q: Why do you do the same thing to both sides of an equation?
faq.a: An equation is like a level pan balance. If you change only one side it tips, so whatever you do to one side you must do to the other.

faq.q: What is the most common mistake with one-step equations?
faq.a: Using the same operation instead of the inverse, for example adding 12 to solve x + 12 = 30. Checking the answer in the original equation catches this mistake.

items.q: The pan balance is level. Each block has the same mass, x. What is x?
items.e: The balance shows x + 25 = 60. Subtract 25 from both sides: x = 60 − 25 = 35. Check: 35 + 25 = 60. Wrong answers: 85 comes from adding 25 instead of subtracting it; 45 comes from taking the smaller digit from the larger in each column.

items.q: The pan balance is level. Each block has the same mass, y. What is y?
items.e: The right pan has 14 + 20 = 34. So y + 9 = 34. Subtract 9 from both sides: y = 34 − 9 = 25. Check: 25 + 9 = 34. Wrong answers: 43 comes from adding 9 instead of subtracting it; 35 comes from taking the smaller digit from the larger in each column.

items.q: The pan balance is level. Each block has the same mass, t. What is t?
items.e: The right pan has 40 + 16 = 56. So 2t = 56. 2t means 2 × t. Divide both sides by 2: t = 56 ÷ 2 = 28. Check: 2 × 28 = 56. Wrong answers: 54 comes from subtracting 2 instead of dividing; 112 comes from multiplying by 2 instead of dividing.

items.q: The balance shows x + 12 = 30. You take 12 off the left pan. What must you do to the right pan to keep it level?
items.e: Whatever you do to one side, do to the other side. Take 12 off the right pan too: x = 30 − 12 = 18. Adding 12 to the right pan would make it tip.

items.q: The balance shows 4x = 28. To find one block, you split the left pan into 4 equal groups. What must you do to the right side?
items.e: Do the same to both sides. Split both sides into 4 equal groups: 28 ÷ 4 = 7, so x = 7. Subtracting 4 undoes + 4, not × 4.

items.q: Which step solves x − 9 = 20 and keeps both sides equal?
items.e: Adding undoes subtracting. Add 9 to both sides: x = 20 + 9 = 29. Check: 29 − 9 = 20. Subtracting 9 again is the same operation, not the inverse.

items.q: Which step solves x ÷ 5 = 6 and keeps both sides equal?
items.e: Multiplying undoes dividing. Multiply both sides by 5: x = 6 × 5 = 30. Check: 30 ÷ 5 = 6. Dividing by 5 again is the same operation.
Substitute x = 6 into each equation. 7 × 6 = 42, so 7x = 42 is true. 6x = 6 has the solution 1.
Substitute x = 12 into each equation. 12 − 4 = 8, so x − 4 = 8 is true. x ÷ 4 = 8 has the solution 32.
Substitute x = 40 into each equation. 40 ÷ 5 = 8, so x ÷ 5 = 8 is true. 8x = 40 has the solution 5, not 40: it mixes up the two numbers.
A number written right before a letter means multiply. 5x means 5 × x, or 5 equal blocks of x. If x = 7, then 5x = 35.

items.e: To check, put the answer back into the equation: 42 + 12 = 54, and 54 is not 30. Arjun added 12 instead of subtracting it. The right answer is 30 − 12 = 18.

items.q: What is the first step to solve x ÷ 9 = 4?
items.e: Multiplication undoes division. Multiply both sides by 9: x = 4 × 9 = 36. Check: 36 ÷ 9 = 4.

sets.title: Write and solve equations from stories

items.q: A Grade 6 class has raised $385 for the Terry Fox Run. Its goal is $1000. Let m be the money it still needs. Which equation matches?
items.e: What they have plus what they still need makes the goal: 385 + m = 1000. Then m = 1000 − 385 = $615.

items.q: 4 SkyTrain cars carry 520 people. Each car carries the same number of people, p. Which equation matches?
items.e: 4 equal groups of p make 520: 4p = 520. Equal groups mean ×, not +. Then p = 520 ÷ 4 = 130.

items.q: A BC Ferries boat has c cars on board. 85 cars drive off and 240 are still on board. Which equation matches?
items.e: Start with c, take away 85, and 240 are left: c − 85 = 240. Then c = 240 + 85 = 325.

items.q: A hiking club in Kamloops splits into 8 equal groups with 12 hikers in each group. Let h be the number of hikers. Which equation matches?
items.e: Start with h hikers and share them into 8 groups to get 12 in each: h ÷ 8 = 12. Then h = 12 × 8 = 96.

items.q: Which equation means “a number divided by 7 is 15”?
items.e: Start with the number n and divide it by 7: n ÷ 7 = 15. Then n = 15 × 7 = 105. 7 ÷ n starts with 7, not with the number.

items.q: Which equation means “6 times a number is 84”?
items.e: “6 times a number” is 6n, and “is 84” is = 84: 6n = 84. Then n = 84 ÷ 6 = 14.

c: 3 tickets cost the same. They cost $45 in all.
$45 is shared and $3 is left over.
A ticket costs $3. Then the price goes up by $45.
items.e: 3x means 3 equal groups of x. 3 tickets at the same price x make $45: 3x = 45, so each ticket costs 45 ÷ 3 = $15.

c: 120 salmon swim up a creek and then 380 more come.
Some salmon swim up a creek. 120 are caught and 380 are left.
380 salmon swim up a creek and 120 are caught.
items.e: x is the number at the start. Take away 120 and 380 are left: x − 120 = 380. Then x = 380 + 120 = 500. The story “380 salmon … 120 are caught” starts with 380, so it matches 380 − 120 = x.
